papers.title: Perioperative Continuation Versus Discontinuation of Antiplatelet Therapy in Colorectal Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Bleeding and Thrombotic Events
papers.authors: Morarasu S, Morarasu B, Guzga E, Sorodoc L, Dimofte G, Lunca S
papers.abstract: Background: Perioperative management of antiplatelet therapy in colorectal surgery requires balancing the risk of surgical bleeding against cardiovascular and cerebrovascular complications after treatment withdrawal. This meta-analysis assessed the safety of continuing antiplatelet therapy compared with preoperative discontinuation. Methods: PubMed and Embase were searched through 30 May 2026 for comparative studies of adults undergoing colorectal surgery. Random-effects models were used to pool odds ratios (ORs) for dichotomous outcomes and mean differences (MDs) for continuous outcomes. The clinically relevant analysis was restricted to patients already receiving antiplatelet therapy with separately reported continuation and discontinuation groups. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I and certainty of evidence with GRADE. Results: Seven observational studies were included in the systematic review, of which four (505 patients; 209 continuation and 296 discontinuation) contributed to the primary analysis. Continuation was not associated with statistically significant differences in postoperative bleeding (OR 2.65, 95% CI 0.78-8.99), thrombotic events (OR 0.29, 95% CI 0.06-1.32), transfusion (OR 1.39, 95% CI 0.35-5.51), overall morbidity (OR 2.08, 95% CI 0.97-4.48), intraoperative blood loss (MD -2.74 mL, 95% CI -13.07 to 7.59), or operative time (MD 0.72 min, 95% CI -11.83 to 13.27). Hospital stay was longer with continuation (MD 0.65 days, 95% CI 0.40-0.91). In the broader secondary analysis, continuation was associated with increased postoperative bleeding (OR 3.30, 95% CI 1.40-7.78). GRADE certainty was very low for all outcomes. Conclusions: Among established antiplatelet users undergoing colorectal surgery, continuation was not associated with statistically significant differences in bleeding or thrombotic outcomes compared with discontinuation. However, sparse events, imprecise estimates, and very low certainty of evidence preclude definitive safety conclusions. Perioperative management should be individualized according to thrombotic risk, anticipated bleeding risk, and surgical complexity.

papers.title: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy plus chemoradiotherapy versus chemoradiotherapy alone for locally advanced rectal cancer: meta-analysis
papers.authors: Lei X, Zhang Y, Wang L, Xie X, Yan M, Li Y
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Standard neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) achieves variable pathological responses. Incorporating immune checkpoint inhibitors into nCRT (inCRT) is a promising intensification strategy, but its efficacy and impact on surgical safety remain poorly defined. This meta-analysis evaluated the oncological benefits and surgical risks of inCRT versus nCRT in both proficient and deficient mismatch repair LARC.
METHODS: A systematic search of the PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library databases was conducted for randomized clinical trials (RCTs) published from inception up to February 2026. The primary outcomes were pathological complete response (pCR) and grade ≥ III severe adverse events (SAEs) according to the Clavien-Dindo complication grading system. Secondary outcomes included major pathological response (MPR) and postoperative complications. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) were calculated using random-effects or fixed-effects models.
RESULTS: Seven RCTs including 1117 patients were identified. Five trials did not restrict enrolment based on mismatch repair or microsatellite instability status, whereas two trials exclusively enrolled patients with mismatch repair-proficient/microsatellite-stable tumours. Although inCRT significantly increased the rate of pCR (31.9% versus 19.3%; RR 1.70; 95% confidence interval (c.i.) 1.37 to 2.10; P < 0.001) and MPR (55.1% versus 40.3%; RR 1.38; 95% c.i. 1.20 to 1.59; P < 0.001) versus nCRT, it was associated with a significantly higher risk of SAEs (30.1% versus 26.8%; RR 1.24; 95% c.i. 1.03 to 1.49; P = 0.02) and overall postoperative complications (32.8% versus 25.6%; RR 1.27; 95% c.i. 1.02 to 1.58; P = 0.03). Subgroup analysis indicated that the pCR benefit was most pronounced in cohorts receiving short-course radiotherapy and consolidation immunotherapy.
CONCLUSION: The addition of immunotherapy to neoadjuvant therapy for LARC markedly improves pathological response but increases high-grade toxicity and surgical morbidity. Although inCRT is a potent intensification strategy, stringent patient selection and regimen optimization are required before widespread adoption.

papers.title: Comparative influence of opioid-free versus opioid-containing anesthetic techniques upon Th1/Th2 balance during laparoscopic colorectal cancer procedures: a randomized controlled trial
papers.authors: Hong L, Wang Y, Cheng Z, Luan H, Zhao Z
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical resection is central to colorectal cancer management, but surgery and anesthesia can induce perioperative immunosuppression. Opioids, a mainstay of perioperative analgesia, may impair cellular immunity, including disruption of Th1/Th2 immune equilibrium. This randomized controlled trial evaluated whether opioid-free anesthesia (OFA) better preserves perioperative immune function than opioid-based anesthesia.
METHODS: Sixty patients scheduled for elective laparoscopic colorectal cancer resection were randomly allocated to OFA (dexmedetomidine, esketamine, lidocaine) or opioid-based anesthesia (sufentanil, remifentanil). Peripheral blood was sampled before induction and on postoperative days 1 and 5 to measure Th1/Th2 ratio, CD4⁺/CD8⁺ ratio and natural killer (NK)-cell counts. Serum cortisol, measures of postoperative pain and complications, including postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), were documented.
RESULTS: On postoperative day 5, the Th1/Th2 ratio was markedly reduced in patients given OFA relative to the control (C) group (1.14 ± 0.40 vs. 1.57 ± 0.89, P = 0.017); in the C group it had returned to baseline, whereas it remained suppressed with OFA. CD4⁺/CD8⁺ ratios and NK-cell counts showed no between-group differences at any point. Cortisol levels at the end of surgery and Numeric Rating Scale pain scores on day 1 were significantly lower with opioid-based anesthesia, while PONV incidence was lower with OFA.
CONCLUSIONS: In laparoscopic colorectal cancer surgery, the OFA regimen used in this trial was associated with sustained postoperative reduction of the Th1/Th2 ratio compared with opioid-based anesthesia. Although OFA reduced PONV, its potential to prolong Th1/Th2 suppression warrants caution when selecting anesthetic strategies for these patients.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial was retrospectively registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry under ChiCTR2500101735 (registered April 29, 2025).

papers.title: Analysis populations and clinical interpretation of outcomes in randomised trials of Hartmann's procedure versus primary anastomosis for perforated diverticulitis
papers.journal_full: Colorectal disease : the official journal of the Association of Coloproctology of Great Britain and Ireland
papers.abstract:
AIM: In randomised trials comparing Hartmann's procedure with primary anastomosis for perforated diverticulitis, stoma reversal and related outcomes may be reported for different analysis populations. This study examined whether analyses of these outcomes represented comparable clinical probabilities.
METHOD: This descriptive meta-research study examined four linked randomised-trial families. Seven clinical and economic reports contributed outcome-specific analyses; a linked protocol supported trial identification. The analysis population, denominator, outcome definition, time origin and horizon, handling of post-randomisation events, and summary measure were extracted for each outcome-specific analysis. The clinical question addressed by each analysis was then reconstructed, and these features were compared across reports.
RESULTS: Early outcomes were generally analysed by initial assignment, whereas later outcomes could be conditioned on survival, stoma formation, reversal, or follow-up availability. In DIVERTI, reported "reversal" percentages (65% and 96%) were complements of definitive-stoma proportions among 18-month survivors, not counts of reversal operations. LADIES/DIVA stoma-free survival instead combined survival and absence of a stoma from the initial strategy. Death could remain in the randomised denominator, enter a longitudinal outcome, or be excluded through survivor-conditioned analyses.
CONCLUSION: In these trials, outcomes used to assess the same surgical decision did not consistently represent the same analysis population or clinical probability. Readers should establish whom each result represents before comparing reversal, stoma-free survival, or reconstructive risk.

papers.title: Preoperative Sarcopenia and Outcomes after Laparoscopic and Robotic Colorectal Cancer Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
papers.authors: Younan M, Meglaa B, Ali M, Tawfeek M, Terra M, Abdelglil M
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preoperative sarcopenia has been increasingly noted as a predictor for outcomes in colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery. However, its impact among patients undergoing minimally invasive CRC resection remains unknown. This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates the relation between preoperative sarcopenia and short-term outcomes after minimally invasive (MIS) CRC surgery.
METHODS: This review followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. A comprehensive literature search through different databases was performed to identify studies assessing adult patients with CRC who underwent minimally invasive colorectal resection. Eligible studies assessed preoperative sarcopenia using objective measures and included a non-sarcopenic comparator group. Pooled odds ratios and their corresponding 95% confidence intervals were estimated; we also used the I² statistic for evaluating heterogeneity.
RESULTS: Eleven studies including 2,453 patients were included, of whom 855 were sarcopenic, and 1,598 were non-sarcopenic. Preoperative sarcopenia showed a higher risk estimate for overall postoperative complications, although the confidence interval crossed the null value (OR 1.92, 95% CI 0.99-3.74; I²=70.1%). A similar pattern was observed for severe complications (OR 1.92, 95% CI 0.80-4.61; I²=63.1%). For surgical site infection, the pooled estimate favored higher odds among patients with preoperative sarcopenia, but the association was not statistically significant under the prespecified random-effects model (OR 1.95, 95% CI 0.70-5.44; I²=61.6%). Anastomotic leakage was not significantly associated with preoperative sarcopenia under the prespecified random-effects model (OR 1.20, 95% CI 0.57-2.51; I²=24.8%).
CONCLUSION: Preoperative sarcopenia, as defined in the included studies, may be associated with adverse short-term outcomes after minimally invasive colorectal cancer surgery. However, the evidence was characterized by substantial heterogeneity, unadjusted estimates, heterogeneous sarcopenia definitions, and very low certainty, limiting conclusions regarding an independent prognostic effect.

papers.title: Distribution and Cytotoxic Potential of NK Cell Subsets in Conventional and Immune-Protective Anesthetic Strategies: A Randomized Study in Colorectal Cancer Patients
papers.authors: de Knijff P, Vulcano T, Jongman R, Olthof C, Struys M, Abdulahad W
papers.abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that anesthesia can modulate natural killer (NK) cell activity, potentially influencing anti-tumor immunity. In this randomized study, 14 patients undergoing laparoscopic colorectal cancer surgery received an immune-protective anesthetic strategy (propofol/epidural/dexmedetomidine) or a conventional strategy (sevoflurane/opioids). Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) were collected preoperatively and at 24 and 48 h postoperatively. CD56+CD16+ NK-cell subsets were characterized by flow cytometry based on NKG2A, NKG2C, and KIR expression. Cytotoxic potential was assessed by intracellular perforin and granzyme B, and CD107a expression as a degranulation marker. Significant decreases from 0 to 48 h were observed in the conventional group for NKG2A+KIR+ double-positive (DP) NK cells (-0.69 percentage points, p = 0.02) and terminally differentiated (NKG2A-NKG2C-) NK cells (-2.22 percentage points, p = 0.02). CD107a expression in DP NK cells increased at 48 h versus baseline (+44.9% MFI, p = 0.04) only in the conventional group. Intracellular granzyme B (-3.38 percentage points; p = 0.02) and perforin levels (-4.56 percentage points, p = 0.04) decreased from 0 to 48 h in the conventional group. These findings suggest that an immune-protective anesthetic strategy may better preserve NK cell subset distribution and cytotoxic potential. However, given the modest magnitude of changes, these results should be interpreted as exploratory.

papers.title: Seed Oils, Dietary Linoleic Acid, and Omega-6 Biomarkers in Adult Health: An Umbrella Review of Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses
papers.authors: Clemente-Suárez V, Yáñez-Sepúlveda R, López-Gil J, Martín-Rodríguez A, Villanueva-Tobaldo C, Tornero-Aguilera J
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Seed oils are widely consumed, yet claims linking linoleic acid (LA) and omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids (n-6 PUFAs) to inflammation and chronic disease remain contentious. We evaluated the evidence in adults while separating named oils, dietary fatty acids, and circulating/tissue biomarkers. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE and Europe PMC were searched to 1 October 2026, with supplementary and citation searches. Adult systematic reviews/meta-analyses were eligible; pregnancy and pediatric populations were excluded. Every synthesis was appraised item by item with AMSTAR 2 (A MeaSurement Tool to Assess systematic Reviews 2) and ROBIS (Risk Of Bias In Systematic reviews) and assigned a confidence tier by a rule defined post hoc, during peer review. Overlap was quantified with the corrected covered area; sensitivity and subgroup analyses examined the Sydney Diet Heart Study, the Minnesota Coronary Experiment, and LA-specific trials. No meta-meta-analysis was performed. The review was not prospectively registered. Results: Thirty-three syntheses were included; the six of higher confidence were not independent (four from one World Health Organization-commissioned program sharing trials). Clinical-endpoint evidence concerned LA/n-6 exposures, largely biomarker-based; named-oil evidence came from short-term trials of intermediate outcomes. Randomized evidence increasing omega-6 showed little or no effect on all-cause mortality (risk ratio [RR] 1.00, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.88-1.12; robust to both trials) or cardiovascular events (RR 0.97, 0.81-1.15; heterogeneity mainly from the Sydney trial), with low certainty; in a hypothesis-generating subgroup, LA-specific trials showed more cardiovascular events than mixed n-6/omega-3 (n-3) trials (RR 1.45 vs. 0.80; two trials each). Prospective dietary/circulating evidence generally showed inverse associations, mostly from overlapping cohorts. LA-rich oils lowered low-density lipoprotein cholesterol when replacing butter (sunflower -0.34 mmol/L per 10% of energy) but differed little from other unsaturated oils, without increasing major inflammatory markers. Cancer findings varied by site and exposure metric, including an ungraded positive dietary LA-colorectal cancer association with an imprecise tissue LA estimate. Conclusions: In adults, the evidence does not support a uniform harmful or beneficial effect of seed oils as a class. Interpretation depends on the oil, replacement nutrient, background n-3 intake, exposure metric, outcome, and design; most evidence is of low certainty, and long-term clinical-outcome evidence for individual oils remains limited.

papers.title: Iliopsoas abscess in crohn's disease: systematic review of case reports and case series
papers.authors: Alawlaqi B, Al-Shabaani A, Al-Shabaani N, Fraihat A, Sayel A, Alghzawi H
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transmural inflammation is a hallmark of Crohn's disease (CD), a chronic inflammatory bowel disease that exposes patients to serious consequences such as fistulas and abscesses. Iliopsoas abscess (IPA) is an uncommon but potentially fatal penetrating (extra-luminal) complication of CD that frequently arises from the direct extension of transmural inflammation into the iliopsoas compartment. Because data on this entity are derived almost exclusively from isolated case reports and small case series, the current literature provides a fragmented understanding of its clinical behaviour, microbiology, and optimal management.
AIM OF THE STUDY: The aim of this study was to summarize the available data on the clinical presentation, diagnostic methods, microbiological profile, treatment plans, and results of IPA in patients with CD by methodically reviewing and analyzing published case reports and case series.
METHODS: This systematic review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251164473) and carried out in accordance with PRISMA 2020 principles. To find relevant studies, a thorough search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar was conducted through February 2025. Case studies and case series describing CD patients who created an IPA were included. Data on demographics, clinical features, diagnostics, microbiology, management, and outcomes were extracted from 53 eligible studies. The Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical assessment methods for case reports and case series were used to evaluate the methodological quality of the included studies.
RESULTS: A total of 53 studies including information on 86 individuals were included, comprising 38 case reports and 15 case series. The mean patient age was 30.5 ± 12.9 years, and 55/86 (64.0%) were male. Fever (25/86; 29.1%), abdominal pain (18/86; 20.9%), and combined hip/flank/back pain (23/86; 26.7%) were the most frequently reported presenting features. Cross-sectional imaging was the cornerstone of diagnosis; CT was the most commonly utilised modality (56/86; 65.1%), followed by ultrasound (55/86; 64.0%) and MRI (52/86; 60.5%); most patients underwent more than one modality during workup. Microbiological data from abscess fluid culture were available in 72/86 patients (83.7%); the majority of isolates were polymicrobial enteric organisms, with Escherichia coli being most frequently identified. Management was typically combined: medical therapy (mainly antibiotics) was documented in 68/86 (79.1%) and surgical or interventional management in 78/86 (90.7%). The overall recovery rate was good, although recurrence was observed-particularly in patients treated with drainage alone without addressing the underlying intestinal disease.
CONCLUSION: IPA is a complication of CD that frequently presents with non-specific symptoms, leading to diagnostic delay. Cross-sectional imaging and a high index of suspicion are essential for early diagnosis. Improving clinical outcomes and preventing recurrence require a multidisciplinary approach that includes aggressive source control through drainage, appropriate antimicrobial therapy, and definitive management of the underlying CD, which frequently includes surgical resection and the subsequent consideration of biologic therapy.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

papers.title: Preoperative prediction of histological types and Ki-67 expression in rectal tumors using time-dependent diffusion MRI quantitative parameters
papers.authors: Li Y, Yi S, Shao C, Ma X, Li H, Chen M
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the clinical value of Time-dependent diffusion MRI (td-dMRI) quantitative parameters in differentiating between rectal neuroendocrine neoplasms (rNEN) and rectal adenocarcinoma (RAC) and in distinguishing between high and low Ki-67 expression in RAC.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This two-center study prospectively enrolled 90 patients with rectal tumors who underwent td-dMRI (January 2024 to March 2025), including 85 with RAC (development cohort, n = 61, validation cohort, n = 24) and 5 with rNEN. The td-dMRI-derived microstructural parameters were estimated using the IMPULSED model, and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) values were measured at different diffusion times. Firth's logistic regression was performed for rNEN-associated parameter selection, while standard logistic regression identified independent predictors to build a combined model for high Ki-67 stratification. Receiver operating characteristic analysis evaluated diagnostic performance. The td-dMRI-derived microstructural parameters were validated against histopathologic measurements.
RESULTS: Significant differences in several td-dMRI parameters were observed between rNENs and RACs, as well as between groups with high and low Ki-67 expression. In the small rNEN cohort, td-dMRI parameters showed promising preliminary diagnostic performance in distinguishing rNEN from RAC (AUC = 0.882). For predicting high Ki-67 expression in RAC, the combined model yielded an AUC of 0.916 in the development cohort and 0.844 in the validation cohort. Microstructural parameters showed strong correlations with histopathology: cell diameter, cellularity, and intracellular volume fraction reached Pearson correlation coefficients (r) of 0.808, 0.773, and 0.765, respectively (all p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Quantitative td-dMRI parameters may serve as a noninvasive tool for evaluating rectal tumor histological types (rNEN vs. RAC) and predicting Ki-67 expression in RAC.

papers.title: Clinical and Molecular Prognostic Factors and Targeted Therapy Outcomes in Colorectal Cancer with Bone and Brain Metastases: A Multicenter Retrospective Turkish Oncology Group Study
papers.authors: Başkurt K, Uyar G, Yeşilbaş E, Büyükşimşek M, Sertesen Çamöz E, Yılmaz E
papers.abstract: Bone and brain metastases are rare in colorectal cancer, and prior studies have treated metastasis as a fixed baseline characteristic. We conducted a multicenter retrospective study of patients with colorectal cancer and bone and/or brain metastases at Turkish Oncology Group centers (May 2011 to September 2025). In multivariable Cox models, the opposite rare-site metastasis and post-metastasis targeted therapy were modeled as time-dependent covariates. Among 188 patients, 139 (73.9%) had bone-first, 33 (17.6%) brain-first, and 16 (8.5%) synchronous disease. Median overall survival was 13.6 months (95% CI 11.6 to 16.4), with no difference by phenotype (p = 0.705). Opposite-site involvement was associated with higher mortality in the bone-metastasis (aHR 2.149, p = 0.006) and brain-metastasis (aHR 2.076, p = 0.018) cohorts, reflecting brain metastasis developing during follow-up in the former and bone metastasis present at diagnosis in the latter. Carcinoembryonic antigen and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio were independently prognostic (both p < 0.01). Anti-EGFR (aHR 0.356, p = 0.001) and anti-VEGF therapy (aHR 0.471, p = 0.005) were associated with lower mortality in patients with bone metastasis but not in those with brain metastasis. Brain metastasis developing in patients with bone metastases carries independent prognostic weight, while targeted-therapy associations in brain metastasis remain inconclusive.

papers.title: Tumor-microbe-microenvironment interactions and therapeutic implications for tumors with intratumoral microbes
papers.authors: Cao Y, Yue J, Ren Y
papers.abstract: The complex interactions between tumors and microbes within the tumor-microbe microenvironment (TMME) are increasingly recognized as critical determinants of tumor progression and therapeutic response. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the presence of intratumoral microbes (ITMs), their routes of entry into tumors, and their functional roles within the TMME, and highlights emerging TMME-targeted strategies for diagnosis and treatment of tumors with ITMs. ITMs can profoundly influence tumor biology by modulating cellular signaling and immune responses, with consequent changes in therapeutic efficacy. For instance, Fusobacterium nucleatum impairs CD8+ T-cell infiltration via succinic acid in drug-resistant colorectal cancer, while cytidine deaminase-expressing bacteria inactivate gemcitabine in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. We summarize the defining characteristics of the TMME, including hypoxia, acidity, and oxidative stress, as well as microbial-associated features such as biofilm formation, bacterial enzymes, and metabolite production. These factors collectively contribute to a dynamic ecosystem that supports microbial persistence and impacts tumor development, immune regulation, and treatment outcomes. Current therapeutic strategies targeting ITM tumors are critically evaluated, including microbial modulation approaches, non-antibiotic modalities, and nanomedicine-based co-delivery systems that combine antibiotics with chemotherapeutics. Co-delivery systems, such as a liposome platform that delivers ciprofloxacin and gemcitabine, allow simultaneous targeting of tumor cells and intratumoral microbes by exploiting the acidic, hypoxic, and enzyme- and metabolite-rich features of the TMME. This TMME-responsive design allows site-specific drug release while eliminating ITMs, and thereby overcomes microbe-induced chemoresistance and enhances therapeutic efficacy. Finally, we highlight the opportunities and challenges associated with TMME-targeted interventions. While modulation or elimination of tumor-associated microbes represents a promising strategy for improving treatment outcomes, significant barriers remain, including a lack of standardized diagnostic tools, microbial heterogeneity, safety concerns, and limited mechanistic understanding of tumor-microbe interactions. Advances in this field will require integrated multi-omics approaches and better translational models for the development of precise, personalized therapies for ITM tumors.

papers.title: Comparative Efficacy of Biologic Therapies for Psoriasis: Insights from Head-to-Head Studies
papers.authors: Rafałowicz A, Nowowiejska-Purpurowicz J, Flisiak I
papers.abstract: Biologic therapies have substantially transformed the management of moderate-to-severe psoriasis, but differences in efficacy, speed of response, durability, and safety reflect the distinct immunological pathways targeted by individual agents. The aim of this review is the analysis and comparison of particular biological agents in terms of efficacy and safety. Head-to-head trials consistently demonstrate that IL-17 and IL-23 inhibitors achieve greater skin clearance than first-generation TNF-α inhibitors. IL-17 blockade, particularly with agents targeting IL-17A, produces rapid clinical improvement by directly suppressing keratinocyte-driven inflammation. Dual IL-17A/IL-17F inhibition with bimekizumab may provide even greater clearance, although broader IL-17 inhibition is associated with a higher frequency of mucosal candidiasis. In contrast, selective IL-23 inhibition acts upstream by suppressing the differentiation and maintenance of pathogenic Th17 cells and appears to provide particularly durable disease control. Selective IL-23 inhibitors may also preserve potentially protective IL-12 signaling, distinguishing them from ustekinumab, which targets the shared p40 subunit. Safety profiles are generally favorable across biologic classes, although mechanism-specific risks include tuberculosis reactivation with TNF-α inhibitors, candidiasis with IL-17 inhibitors, and inflammatory bowel disease concerns with IL-17 blockade. Therefore, biologic selection should be individualized according to disease severity, required speed and durability of response, comorbidities, affected anatomical sites, safety considerations, dosing frequency, patient preferences and adherence goals. Current comparative evidence supports increasingly targeted approaches within the IL-23/IL-17 axis.

papers.title: Severity ranking of immunocompromise conditions for patients undergoing emergency surgery: an outcomes-based reassessment of the 2021 consensus classification system published in the World Journal of Emergency Surgery
papers.journal_full: World journal of emergency surgery : WJES
papers.authors: Kennedy G, Allen G, Davidson G, Liu C, Hantouli M, Flum D
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In 2021, the World Journal of Emergency Surgery published consensus guidelines classifying immunocompromised patients with acute abdomen into "mild-moderate" and "severe" immune deficiency categories to standardize perioperative risk assessment and guide surgical decision-making. We assessed whether published mortality and complication data are consistent with this classification.
METHODS: We conducted a structured literature review of PubMed and MEDLINE (2000-2025) for studies reporting mortality and complications in adult immunocompromised patients undergoing emergency colectomy, cholecystectomy, appendectomy, or small bowel resection, with a non-immunocompromised control group. Of the fifteen immunocompromising conditions in the classification, three were excluded for confounding or insufficient data (burns, trauma, post-splenectomy) and two pairs combined (symptomatic HIV/AIDS with CD4 < 200 cells/mm3; malignancy with and without chemotherapy), yielding ten categories. For each, we calculated procedure-specific relative mortality and complication rates. We defined a severe-risk threshold of greater than 3 × mortality and tested concordance at alternative thresholds (2-4 ×) in a sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: The guidelines classified five conditions as severe (neutropenia, steroid use, HIV < 200 cells/mm3, malignancy, transplant) and five as mild-moderate (uremia, advanced age, malnutrition, diabetes, HIV > 200 cells/mm3). Among the severe conditions, three (neutropenia, steroid use, HIV < 200 cells/mm3) showed greater than 3 × mortality risk, with neutropenia highest (~ 12 ×); the other two (malignancy 2-3 × , transplant 1-2 ×) showed only mild-moderate excess risk. Among the mild-moderate conditions, two (uremia 6-7 × , advanced age 2-9 ×) showed excess mortality and complication risk more consistent with severe immunocompromise.
CONCLUSION: Observed procedure-specific mortality and complication data do not consistently support the 2021 consensus severity ranking: four of the ten conditions were discordant with their assigned classification. This analysis suggests reconsidering uremia and advanced age as severe, and malignancy and transplant as mild-moderate. Because immunocompromise severity may influence whether and when patients undergo surgery, these findings highlight a priority for evidence-based refinement of severity ranking in emergency general surgery.

papers.title: The gut microbiome and brain inflammation in Parkinson's disease: mechanisms and therapies
papers.authors: Shah A, Truong T, Savani E, Shi H, Komandooru D, Jayakumar N
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most common chronic progressive neurodegenerative disorder affecting over 10 million people worldwide. PD is increasingly understood to have peripheral origins in a substantial subset of patients, in whom microbiota dysbiosis precedes and facilitates central neurodegeneration via the gut-brain axis. Dysbiosis-associated depletion of short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-producing bacteria, enrichment of lipopolysaccharide-producing taxa, and loss of gut barrier integrity activate toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) signaling, prime microglia towards a disease-linked phenotype, and promote the misfolding of α-synuclein and its propagation from the enteric to the central nervous system. Complement, activated by α-synuclein and shaped by the gut microbiota, further links dysbiosis to neurodegeneration. Beyond neuroinflammation, the gut microbiome modulates levodopa pharmacokinetics through bacterial tyrosine decarboxylase activity and interacts with catechol-O-methyltransferase inhibitors to alter drug bioavailability. Certain microbial metabolites, including the trimethylamine N-oxide to butyrate ratio and secondary bile acids, have emerged as candidate biomarkers. Cutaneous phosphorylated α-synuclein deposition and seeding amplification assays (SAA) are evaluated as minimally invasive peripheral biomarkers, along with epidemiological evidence linking prior antibiotic exposure and inflammatory bowel disease to PD risk. Emerging therapeutic strategies include SCFA supplementation, fecal microbiota transplantation, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) agonists, and targeted probiotics. Microbiome-direct strategies may benefit patients with a gut-first PD subtype, suggested by prodromal constipation, rapid eye movement (REM) sleep behavior disorder, or cardiac sympathetic denervation, underscoring the need for subtype-stratified trial designs. In this review article, we highlight recent evidence linking the gut microbiome with neuroinflammation in Parkinson's disease through α-synuclein pathology, complement activation, and LPS/TLR4/NF-κB signaling, and discuss the implications for biomarkers, pharmacological interactions, and therapies. In conclusion, the convergence of mechanisms, biomarkers, and clinical evidence indicates the gut microbiome may be a significant diagnostic and modifiable therapeutic target in PD.

papers.title: Insights on Intestinal Fibrosis: From Stromal Cell Heterogeneity and Metabolic Reprogramming to Novel Therapeutic Strategies
papers.authors: Liu Y, Wang J, Xu R, Bai X, Zhang Y, Bi X
papers.abstract: Intestinal fibrosis is a major complication of inflammatory bowel disease, and it can lead to fixed strictures, intestinal obstruction, and repeated surgical intervention. Although effective control of inflammation may limit ongoing tissue injury, no approved therapy selectively prevents or reverses established intestinal fibrosis. This therapeutic gap reflects an incomplete understanding of the cellular and metabolic mechanisms that sustain fibrotic remodeling. In this review, we integrate classical extracellular-matrix pathways with recent single-cell, spatial, and metabolic evidence to provide a multicellular framework for intestinal fibrogenesis. Single-cell studies indicate that intestinal fibroblasts comprise overlapping and environmentally responsive states rather than fixed lineages. Their activation is shaped by reciprocal communication with immune cells, epithelial and endothelial cells, smooth muscle cells, creeping fat, and the intestinal microbiota. Metabolic reprogramming provides an additional layer of regulation through glycolysis, pentose phosphate pathway, glutamine-proline metabolism, lactate-associated signaling, and extracellular metabolite sensing. However, the strength of evidence varies among these mechanisms, and direct links between defined fibroblast states and specific metabolic dependencies remain limited. In this review, we further discuss therapeutic opportunities targeting immune-stromal communication, pathogenic fibroblast programs, cellular metabolism, extracellular-matrix turnover, and mechanotransduction. Translating these opportunities into stage-specific interventions will require spatially resolved functional models to validate causal targets and fibrosis-selective biomarkers to assess therapeutic effects.

papers.title: Current Landscape in Clinical Drug Repurposing: From Non-Oncology Drugs to New Cancer Applications
papers.authors: Bivacqua R, Barreca M, Raimondi F, Giuffrida S, Lo Mascolo F, Spanò V
papers.abstract: Drug repurposing builds on pharmacological and safety information already available for an approved drug, but this advantage requires additional studies to establish the biological effect and related mechanisms of action. We conducted a clinically focused review of non-oncology drugs tested as active cancer treatments in interventional studies from 1 January 2021 to 31 July 2026. Randomized trials, phase II-III studies, biomarker-selected cohorts, and studies reporting pharmacokinetics or human target engagement were prioritized. Despite the large number of registered studies, the landscape is still dominated by early-phase, academically sponsored trials. Several widely studied candidates, including metformin, nelfinavir, disulfiram-copper, losartan, and propofol, were negative in randomized evaluations. Conversely, aspirin reduced recurrence in localized colorectal cancer with PI3K-pathway alterations, while preoperative peritumoral lidocaine administration was associated with improved disease-free survival and overall survival in a randomized breast cancer trial. Smaller randomized trials investigating pharmacological ascorbate in pancreatic cancer and simvastatin in recurrent small-cell lung cancer provided preliminary efficacy signals that require confirmation in larger studies. Across drug classes, unsuccessful programs were often limited by inadequate exposure, uncertain tumor penetration, absent pharmacodynamic evidence, heterogeneous patient populations, or weak continuity between exploratory and confirmatory development. Progress will depend on more selective clinical hypotheses, early demonstration of human pharmacology, prospective biomarkers, and clear regulatory ownership.

papers.title: Microbiota-Driven Mechanisms in Endometrial Cancer Pathogenesis: Focus on Lynch Syndrome
papers.authors: Actis S, Cazzaniga M, D'Alonzo M, Perrini G, Giorgi M, Pace L
papers.abstract: Lynch syndrome is the most common hereditary syndrome predisposing to endometrial cancer, but the mechanisms contributing to tumor development remain incompletely understood. This review aimed to summarise current evidence on the composition and potential pathogenic role of the microbiota in Lynch syndrome-associated endometrial cancer and to explore its clinical implications. A systematic literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Embase was conducted between October and November 2025 using predefined terms related to microbiota, carcinogenesis, endometrial cancer, and Lynch syndrome. Available evidence suggests that alterations in the microbiota may contribute to carcinogenesis through chronic inflammation, immune modulation, metabolic changes, and bacterial genotoxicity. Studies in Lynch syndrome carriers with endometrial or colorectal cancer report an increased abundance of potentially pro-inflammatory Gram-negative bacteria, including Bacteroides fragilis and Fusobacterium nucleatum, together with a reduction in short-chain fatty acid-producing bacteria such as Faecalibacterium, Blautia, and Butyrivibrio. Microbial metabolites, including butyrate, may have protective effects, whereas bacterial β-glucuronidase activity may increase estrogen bioavailability and contribute to a tumor-promoting environment. Emerging evidence also suggests that the microbiota may influence treatment response and toxicity. Overall, current evidence supports a potential role for the microbiota in Lynch syndrome-associated endometrial carcinogenesis, although data remain limited. Further studies are needed to determine whether microbiota profiling could contribute to risk stratification, prevention, and personalized therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Decision-Linked Multimodal Prediction in Non-Metastatic Rectal Adenocarcinoma
papers.authors: Mwazha A, Kader S, Naicker N, Mhemedi B, Mazibuko Z, Mtembu T
papers.abstract: Treatment options for non-metastatic rectal adenocarcinoma include total neoadjuvant therapy, selective radiotherapy omission, watch-and-wait, and mismatch-repair-guided immunotherapy. Prediction studies often conflate pathological and clinical complete response, radiological regression, organ preservation, local regrowth, and survival. This structured narrative review evaluated multimodal assessments by clinical decision and timing. MEDLINE/PubMed, Estudies andcopus were searched for literature published from 1 January 2015 to 30 June 2026, supplemented by guidelines, citation tracking, landmark earlier studies, and separately identified contextual sources. Evidence was organized around baseline selection, restaging, postoperative risk, and surveillance. An author-derived four-tier framework distinguished evidence maturity from implementation feasibility. Baseline pelvic magnetic resonance imaging and mismatch repair/microsatellite instability testing provided the most actionable pretreatment information. Concordant imaging, endoscopy, and digital rectal examination supported clinical complete-response assessment and watch-and-wait only with intensive surveillance and timely salvage surgery. Resection histopathology defined residual disease and postoperative risk but could not retrospectively justify surgery omission. Carcinoembryonic antigen remained an established adjunct. Circulating tumor DNA, radiomics, immune and stromal measures, molecular signatures, and artificial intelligence models require further validation before independently directing treatment. Clinical usefulness depends on alignment with a defined decision, time point, and endpoint. The optimal pathway delivers feasible, validated information when it can safely change care.
